faqs.q: How do I merge multiple PDF files?
faqs.a: Upload 2 to 20 PDF files to the Merge PDF tool, then click Merge. Your files are combined into a single PDF in upload order, ready to download.

faqs.q: How many PDF files can I merge at once?
faqs.a: You can merge between 2 and 20 PDF files in a single job. Each file can be up to 50MB.

faqs.q: Will merging PDFs reduce their quality?
faqs.a: No. Merging only rearranges pages into one file — the content, images, and text of each PDF are preserved exactly as they were.

faqs.q: Can I merge a password-protected PDF?
faqs.a: Password-protected PDFs must be unlocked first. Use the Unlock PDF tool with the correct password, then merge the unlocked file.

faqs.q: Is it free to merge PDFs online?

faqs.q: How do I split a PDF into separate files?

faqs.q: What page range format should I use?
faqs.a: Use 1-based page numbers with commas and dashes, for example 1-3,5,8-10. This extracts pages 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, and 10.

faqs.q: Can I split a PDF into individual pages?
faqs.a: Yes. Select the 'every' mode and each page of your PDF becomes a separate PDF file inside the ZIP download.

faqs.q: Is there a page limit for splitting?

faqs.q: Can I convert only some pages to images?

faqs.q: What does OCR do to a PDF?
faqs.a: OCR (optical character recognition) analyzes the images in a scanned PDF, recognizes the text, and embeds an invisible text layer. The pages look the same, but the text becomes searchable and selectable.

faqs.q: How long does OCR take?
faqs.a: It depends on page count and content — scanned pages are processed individually. Pages that already have text are skipped instantly, so mixed documents finish much faster.

faqs.q: Which languages are supported?
faqs.a: Set the language option with a Tesseract language code such as eng for English or eng+deu for English and German combined.

faqs.q: Will OCR change how my pages look?
faqs.a: No. The original scanned images are kept as the visible pages; only an invisible text layer is added underneath.

faqs.q: My PDF already has some text. Will it be re-OCRed?
faqs.a: No — pages with a usable text layer are detected and copied through unchanged. Only image-only pages go through recognition.

faqs.a: Metadata is hidden information stored in the PDF: title, author, subject, keywords, creation date, the software that made it, page count, and whether it's encrypted.

faqs.q: Can I see if a PDF is password protected?
faqs.a: Yes — the metadata view includes the document's encryption status.

faqs.q: Is the metadata always accurate?
faqs.a: It reflects what the PDF's creator stored in the file. Some PDFs have empty or generic metadata if the authoring software didn't fill it in.

faqs.q: Will editing metadata affect my document's content?

faqs.q: Why does PDF metadata matter?

faqs.q: What happens if I forget the password?

faqs.q: What kind of encryption is used?

faqs.a: Upload the protected PDF, enter its password, and click Unlock. You'll get a normal PDF with no password prompt.

faqs.a: No. You must know the correct password — this tool removes protection from files you have the right to access; it cannot crack unknown passwords.

faqs.q: Why would I unlock a PDF?
faqs.a: Other tools refuse locked files for safety. Unlocking first lets you merge, split, compress, or convert the document normally.

faqs.a: The matched text is covered with opaque black rectangles in the output PDF. For maximum safety with highly sensitive material, verify the output before distributing.

faqs.q: What does flattening a PDF do?
faqs.a: Flattening renders every page to a full-page image. Annotations, comments and filled form values are baked into the image first, so they stay visible — but nothing in the output can be edited, selected or searched anymore.

faqs.q: Why should I flatten a filled form?
faqs.a: An unflattened form's values can still be edited by anyone with a PDF editor. Flattening locks the filled-in values into an image.

faqs.q: Will flattening change how my PDF looks?
faqs.a: The pages look the same, but they are now images: text can no longer be selected or searched, and text-heavy PDFs may get bigger. Choose 150 DPI if file size matters more than print sharpness.

faqs.q: How much can I crop from a PDF page?
faqs.a: As much as you like, as long as some of the page remains. If the trim amounts would remove the entire page width or height, the tool stops with an error instead of producing an empty page.

faqs.q: What unit are the crop amounts in?
faqs.a: Points — the standard PDF unit. 72 points equal 1 inch, so trimming 36 points removes half an inch from that edge.

faqs.q: Does cropping delete the trimmed content permanently?
faqs.a: Cropping adjusts each page's visible crop box. The hidden content is not rewritten, so for permanent removal of sensitive content use the Redact tool instead.

faqs.q: Why is the text in my grayscale PDF not selectable?
faqs.a: To guarantee a true grayscale result, each page is rendered as a grayscale image. That means text becomes part of the picture — it prints identically but can no longer be selected or searched. Keep a copy of the original if you need the text layer.

faqs.q: Which DPI should I choose?
faqs.a: 150 DPI is fine for on-screen reading, 200 DPI balances size and clarity, and 300 DPI or more is best for printing. Higher DPI means larger files.

faqs.q: Will grayscale make my PDF smaller?
faqs.a: Usually yes for colour, image-heavy documents, because colour information is dropped. Text-only PDFs may grow slightly because pages become images — the Compress tool is better for those.
